execution_steps: 1. Continuing the FF6 mission after event 269's exact_next_action -- checked whether the pinned .local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/ cache already contains the core XSD schema text, since Glossary/Validation/sizeRestriction's own module schemas had all been found embedded verbatim in the same spec document this session.

2. Found the pinned XLIFF 2.1 spec's own Appendix A.3 'Core XML Schema' section (.local/format-contracts/acquired/xliff/src-xliff-003.bin, lines 3230-3657) contains the FULL, complete, normative core schema, the spec's own words describing it as 'listed below for reading convenience' -- the authoritative text, not a summary or approximation.

3. Extracted the schema programmatically (sliced the exact <pre> block boundaries, HTML-unescaped </>/&), wrote it to a scratch file, and verified it parses as valid XSD via a locally-installed xmlschema library before committing to building anything against it.

4. Confirmed network access works in this environment (pip install --dry-run succeeded), installed xmlschema==4.1.0 -- EXACTLY the version already declared in pyproject.toml's own 'schema' extra, not a new/different dependency choice.

5. Confirmed xmlschema ships its own bundled copy of the standard, unversioned W3C xml.xsd (for the xml: namespace xml:lang/xml:space/xml:id), so the schema's own <xs:import> of that namespace resolves automatically with zero network access at validation time -- verified by successfully parsing the schema and validating real documents against it.

6. Bundled the extracted schema at src/format_factory/xliff/validation/xliff_core_2.0.xsd, added it to pyproject.toml's package-data table, built a real wheel via `pip wheel .`, and confirmed the .xsd ships inside it byte-identical to the source file before writing any Python code that depends on it.

7. Added errors.py::SchemaValidationUnavailable (a new XliffError subclass) and validation/schema_validator.py::schema_validate(), lazily importing xmlschema inside a function (not at module top-level) so the rest of the package remains fully installable and functional with zero xmlschema installed.
8. Wired schema_validate and SchemaValidationUnavailable into validation/__init__.py and the top-level package __init__.py/__all__.
9. Ran the pre-existing xliff suite (517 passed) BEFORE writing any new test, confirming zero regressions from the wiring alone.

10. Probed interactively: a valid document validates cleanly; a document missing required attributes at two different nesting levels reports BOTH violations (not just the first); diagnostics carry a structural path; simulating an ImportError for xmlschema (via a temporary builtins.__import__ patch) raises the new SchemaValidationUnavailable with a clear message rather than crashing.

11. Wrote 6 new tests, using pytest.importorskip('xmlschema') at module level (matching the existing zst/conftest.py precedent for optional native dependencies) plus one dedicated test exercising the graceful-degradation path via monkeypatch, carefully clearing the module-level lru_cache before and after to avoid leaking simulated-absence state into other tests.

12. Ran the full xliff suite (517 -> 523 passed), ruff, and mypy --strict on the full xliff source tree (added a TYPE_CHECKING-guarded import to satisfy strict mode's return-type requirement without needing xmlschema type stubs) -- all clean.
13. Ran the combined 6-format regression suite (3532 -> 3538 passed, same 4 pre-existing unrelated safetensors interop failures, 2 skipped) -- zero regression beyond the 6 new tests.

14. Updated both obligations' evidence: NARROWED (not closed, since the compound rule_text's third clause -- module-schema composition -- remains genuinely unbuilt) missing_behavior to remove the 'no schema files bundled... never imported' claim while keeping the module-schema/Schematron gap honestly documented; added the 6 new tests to positive/negative selectors, added XLIFF-CORE-SCHEMA-VALIDATION-PROOF to execution_evidence_ids. Both obligations correctly stay partial.
